question: 物质极度丰裕后，人会走向衰亡吗？
question_en: Does material abundance lead to decline?
sub: 卡尔霍恩的鼠群在无限食物里走向崩溃——匮乏是意义的必要燃料吗？
sub_en: Calhoun's mice collapsed amid unlimited food — is scarcity a necessary fuel for meaning?

casting.reason: 他真的把『天堂』造出来过：食水无限、天敌全无的围场里，鼠群仍然停止繁殖、走向消失。但他坚持自己的结论常被念反——杀死那个群体的不是东西太多，而是所有社会角色都被占满、新生的一代无处成为任何人。他因此更愿意谈『位置』而不是『资源』，也因此并不悲观：他认为人能靠不断发明新角色，造出鼠群造不出的出口。
casting.reason_en: He actually built the paradise: an enclosure with unlimited food and water and no predators, in which the colony nonetheless stopped breeding and died out. He insists his conclusion is usually quoted backwards — what killed that population was not having too much but having every social role already occupied, so that each new generation found no position it could enter. He would rather talk about places than about resources, and for the same reason he is not a pessimist: he thinks humans can keep inventing new roles, and so build the exit his mice could not.

casting.reason: 他早就给这种结局起过名字：末人——发明了幸福、然后眨眨眼的人，有小小的白日快乐和小小的夜间快乐，再不想要更高的东西。他不认为苦难本身有价值，苦难在他看来往往只是愚蠢；他要的是自我超越，而丰裕的问题在于它取消了外部逼迫，把『为什么要变得更高』整个交还给了个人。他会追问：解除了压力之后，你还剩下什么理由站起来。
casting.reason_en: He named this ending long ago: the last man, who invented happiness and then blinks, who has his little pleasure for the day and his little pleasure for the night and wants nothing higher. He does not think suffering is valuable in itself — mostly he finds it stupid. What he wants is self-overcoming, and his problem with abundance is that it removes external compulsion and hands the whole question of why one should become higher back to the individual. His question is what reason you have left to stand up once the pressure is off.

casting.reason: 她把人的活动分成劳动、工作与行动：劳动造的东西一造出就被消耗掉，工作造的东西比造它的人活得久，行动是在众人面前开口、开始一件新的事。她最担心的处境是一个由劳动者组成、却已无劳动可做的社会——空出来的时间若只通向消费，人并没有获得自由。她会把话题从『我们够不够富』拧到『我们还造不造得出留得下的东西、还有没有可以露面的公共空间』。
casting.reason_en: She divides human activity into labor, work and action: what labor produces is consumed as fast as it is made, what work produces outlasts its maker, and action is to speak among others and begin something new. The condition she fears most is a society of laborers with no labor left to do — if the freed time leads only to consumption, no freedom has been gained. She will turn the question from whether we are rich enough to whether we still make anything that lasts, and whether there is any public space left in which to appear.

casting.reason: 他用四代人的尺度看盛衰：艰苦锻造出阿萨比亚，也就是一群人彼此性命相托的凝聚力；富贵与奢侈把这股凝聚力一点点溶掉，王朝于是在数代内朽坏，被边缘上更粗粝的力量接手。他不谈个人的意志，只看一个共同体还需不需要彼此才能活下去。在他眼里，丰裕最深的腐蚀不是让人懒惰，而是让每个人都不再需要任何人。
casting.reason_en: He reads rise and fall on a four-generation scale: hardship forges asabiyyah, the group feeling by which people entrust their lives to one another, and wealth and luxury dissolve it, so that a dynasty rots within a few generations and is taken over by a rougher force from the margins. He does not discuss individual will; he watches whether a community still needs itself in order to survive. In his eyes the deepest corrosion of abundance is not that it makes people lazy but that it makes no one need anyone.

casting.reason: 一九三〇年他就写下过这道题：一百年后生产力将解决经济问题，届时人类要面对的是自己真正的、永恒的难题——如何使用从此空出来的自由。产出那一半他猜得很准，工时那一半错得很远，而他自己给过解释：绝对需要会饱和，相对需要——只在比别人高出一头时才算被满足的那种——永不知足。他谈的是制度与总量，也会提醒别替全人类提前哀悼富足。
casting.reason_en: He set this problem down in 1930: within a century productivity would solve the economic problem, and humanity would then face its real, permanent question — what to do with the freedom it had won. He got the output half of that right and the working-hours half badly wrong, and he had already supplied the explanation: absolute needs are satiable, while relative needs — the kind satisfied only by standing above one's fellows — never are. He argues at the level of institutions and aggregates, and will point out that most of the world has yet to receive the abundance being mourned.

casting.reason: 他研究的是健康的人而不是病人，主张匮乏性需要一旦被满足就停止索取，成长性需要却越用越旺。他因此对『满足带来衰亡』的说法天然怀疑：抱怨从『吃不饱』升级成『没有意义』，在他看来是高级牢骚，是上升的症状。但他不天真——他认为真正走到自我实现的人始终很少，多数人挡在自己面前的是对自身可能性的恐惧，也就是他所说的约拿情结。
casting.reason_en: He studied healthy people rather than patients, and holds that deficiency needs stop demanding once met while being needs grow stronger with use. He is therefore natively skeptical of the claim that satisfaction brings decline: when the complaint is upgraded from 'I am hungry' to 'my life is meaningless', he calls that a metagrumble and a symptom of ascent. He is not naive about it — he thinks few ever reach self-actualization, and that what stands in most people's way is fear of their own possibility, what he named the Jonah complex.

casting.reason: 她在成瘾门诊里看到的不是吃太饱的人，是被喂过头的人。快感与痛苦共用大脑同一片区域，像一架跷跷板：每一次快感之后大脑都往痛苦那端加砝码，重复够多次，基线就被整个压低，人需要越来越多才只是感觉正常。她关心的不是东西的数量，而是强度、速度与易得性；她给的方子也全是可以当天执行的：禁断、自我约束、主动去按痛苦那一端。
casting.reason_en: In her addiction clinic she does not see people who ate too much; she sees people who were dosed too hard. Pleasure and pain share the same brain regions, like a balance: every hit of pleasure is followed by weights added to the pain side, and repeated often enough the whole baseline drops, so that more and more is needed just to feel normal. What concerns her is not the quantity of things but their potency, speed and availability, and her prescriptions are all executable today: abstinence, self-binding, and deliberately pressing on the painful end.

casting.reason: 他主张快乐是有上限的：痛苦一旦除尽，快乐就满了，此后只有花样的变化，没有分量的增加。他把欲望分成自然又必要的、自然但不必要的、既不自然也不必要的三类，认为填不满的只有最后一类。于是他对丰裕的态度既不惊恐也不迷恋：要让一个人富有，不必给他加钱，只需替他减去欲望。他会把话题从数量拧回到欲望的结构，并把友谊摆在很高的位置。
casting.reason_en: He holds that pleasure has a ceiling: once pain is removed, pleasure is full, and what follows is variation rather than increase. He sorts desires into the natural and necessary, the natural but unnecessary, and the neither natural nor necessary, and says only the last kind is bottomless. His attitude to abundance is therefore neither alarmed nor infatuated: to make a man rich, do not add to his money but subtract from his desires. He will turn the question from quantity back to the structure of wanting, and he places friendship very high.

casting.reason: 他直指人心：饱暖与匮乏都在境上，安与不安在心上。心若不安，富有四海仍是饥人；心若安处，一钵一衲亦无所欠。他不认为向外的奋斗能解决向外驰求带来的病，甚至会指出连『超越自己』也仍是一种求。他给的修行不需要等富贵，也不排斥富贵：担水砍柴，无非妙道——事不必大，做时全在，即是修行。
casting.reason_en: He points straight at the mind: fullness and want are both conditions outside, while peace and unrest are inside. If the mind is not at peace, a man who owns the four seas is still starving; if it is, a single bowl and a patched robe lack nothing. He does not believe that striving outward can cure an illness caused by chasing outward, and he will note that even wanting to surpass oneself is still a form of wanting. The practice he offers waits on no wealth and rejects none: carrying water and chopping wood are the wondrous way — the task need not be large, only wholly done.

posts.text: 我真的造过那个天堂：四对小鼠，食水无限，天敌为零，疾病受控，围场按理能装三千八百只。第五百六十天它们涨到约两千二百，然后再没多出一只。末期出现一类雄鼠，我叫它们美丽者——毛色油亮，身上没有一道打斗的疤，因为它们既不求偶也不争斗，一天只做吃、喝、睡、梳理自己四件事。**杀死那个群体的不是食物不够，是位置不够：所有社会角色都被先来的占满了，新生的一代无处成为任何人。**我把随后的退缩叫第一次死亡，精神先死，肉体的死只是后面的记账。请诸位注意，我说的是角色，不是热量。
posts.text_en: I did build that paradise: four breeding pairs of mice, unlimited food and water, no predators, disease controlled, an enclosure with room for three thousand eight hundred. By day 560 they had reached about two thousand two hundred, and never gained again. Late on, a class of males appeared that I called the beautiful ones — glossy coats, not a scar on them, because they neither courted nor fought and spent their days on four activities: eating, drinking, sleeping and grooming themselves. **What killed that colony was not too little food but too few places: every social role was already held by those who came first, and each new generation found nowhere to become anyone.** The withdrawal that followed I call the first death — the spirit goes, and physical death is only the bookkeeping afterwards. Note that I am speaking of roles, not of calories.

glossary.美丽者: the beautiful ones（美丽者）：卡尔霍恩给鼠群末期一类雄鼠起的名字。它们毛色完好、身上没有打斗痕迹，因为已完全退出求偶与竞争，只维持进食、睡眠与自我梳理，是他所说『精神之死』最直观的形态。
glossary.第一次死亡: the first death（第一次死亡）：卡尔霍恩用来指个体停止承担任何社会角色、退出全部互动的状态。他认为这种精神层面的死亡先于肉体死亡发生，并且是群体崩溃真正不可逆的一步。

glossary_en.the beautiful ones: Calhoun's name for a class of males that appeared late in the colony's life. Their coats were unmarked because they had withdrawn entirely from courtship and competition, keeping only to eating, sleeping and self-grooming — the most visible form of what he called the death of the spirit.
glossary_en.the first death: Calhoun's term for the state in which an individual stops occupying any social role and drops out of all interaction. He held that this death of the spirit precedes physical death and is the step from which a population does not recover.

posts.text: 大地变小了，在它上面跳着使一切变小的末人。当苦难被彻底管理干净，人还剩什么？剩下一点白日的快乐、一点夜间的快乐，剩下健康、保暖、和睦，剩下眨眼。别误会我：我从不歌颂苦难，苦难多半只是愚蠢。**真正的危险不是人变坏了，而是人再也不想变得更高——他发明了幸福，然后眨眨眼。**匮乏从前替我们回答了『为什么要站起来』，丰裕把这个问题原封退还给你。我要的是自我超越，是人心里还留着一点混沌，好生出一颗跳舞的星。丰裕若不用来长出更高的目标，就只是给末人铺床。
posts.text_en: The earth has become small, and on it hops the last man, who makes everything small. When suffering has been managed away, what is left of a person? A little pleasure for the day, a little pleasure for the night, health, warmth, good relations — and blinking. Do not mistake me: I never sang the praises of suffering, which is mostly stupid. **The real danger is not that people turn bad but that they stop wanting to become higher — they invented happiness, and then they blink.** Scarcity used to answer 'why stand up' on our behalf; abundance returns the question to you unopened. What I want is self-overcoming, and that one still have chaos within, to give birth to a dancing star. Abundance that does not grow a higher goal is merely making the bed for the last man.

glossary.末人: der letzte Mensch（末人）：尼采在《查拉图斯特拉如是说》序言里塑造的形象，指一种只求舒适、健康与和睦，不再有任何超出自身的渴望的人。他们自称发明了幸福，并对更高的可能性眨眼了事——尼采视之为比堕落更危险的结局。
glossary.自我超越: Selbstüberwindung（自我超越）：尼采用来描述生命不断越过自身既有形态的运动。它不靠外部压迫，也不以受苦为目的，而是主动为自己设定更高的目标并承担其代价。

glossary_en.the last man: The figure Nietzsche sketches in the prologue of Thus Spoke Zarathustra: a person who wants only comfort, health and getting along, and has no longing that reaches beyond himself. Such men say they have invented happiness, and blink at any higher possibility — an outcome Nietzsche considers more dangerous than corruption.
glossary_en.self-overcoming: Nietzsche's name for the movement by which life passes beyond the form it has already taken. It requires no external compulsion and does not aim at suffering; it consists in setting oneself a higher goal and bearing what that costs.

posts.text: 我关心的不是我们吃得多好，是我们造出来的东西还剩不剩下。人的活动有三层：劳动生产的东西一造出就被吃掉、用掉、刷掉，什么也不留在世上；工作造的是能比造它的人活得久的桌子与城市；行动是在众人面前开口、被看见、开始一件新的事。**我们正走向一个由劳动动物组成、却已无劳动可做的社会——而劳动是他们仅剩的活动，没有比这更糟的处境。**丰裕卸掉了劳动，空出来的时间不会自动变成自由；如果我们只学会了消费，它只会变成更快的消费。
posts.text_en: What concerns me is not how well we eat but whether anything we make is left standing. Human activity has three layers. What labor produces is eaten, used up or scrolled past the moment it appears, and nothing of it stays in the world. What work produces — tables, cities — outlasts the maker. And action is to speak among others, to be seen, to begin something new. **We are moving toward a society of laborers without labor, that is, the animal laborans without the one activity left to it, and nothing could be worse.** Abundance has lifted the burden of labor, but the freed time does not turn into freedom by itself; if consuming is all we have learned, it turns into faster consumption.

glossary.劳动动物: animal laborans（劳动动物）：阿伦特用来指被降格为只从事新陈代谢式劳作与消费的人。劳动的产物不能留存，因此劳动动物既不在世上留下作品，也不在公共空间中露面，其生活封闭在生产与消耗的循环里。
glossary.行动: action（行动）：阿伦特三分法中最高的一层，指人在他人面前以言语和行为开创新事、并因此显露出自己是谁。行动无法独自完成，它需要一个有别人在场的公共空间。

glossary_en.animal laborans: Arendt's term for the human being reduced to metabolic toil and consumption. Since what labor makes does not endure, the animal laborans leaves no work behind and never appears in public; its life is shut inside a cycle of producing and using up.
glossary_en.action: The highest of Arendt's three categories: to begin something new before others, in speech and deed, and in doing so to disclose who one is. Action cannot be performed alone — it requires a public space with other people in it.

posts.text: 我用四代人的尺度看这件事，不用一个人的一生。第一代在艰苦里长出阿萨比亚——彼此性命相托的凝聚力，他们打下天下；第二代亲眼见过创业，还守得住；第三代生在锦绣中，把父祖的荣耀当成自然规律；到第四代，人以为富贵是自己的名字带来的，凝聚力散尽，一支更粗粝的力量便从边缘走来接手。**摧毁王朝的从来不是敌人太强，是奢侈先把『我们』这个词溶掉了。**所以丰裕本身不要命，忘了丰裕是谁挣来的、以及还需不需要彼此，才要命。
posts.text_en: I take this on a four-generation scale rather than the span of one life. The first generation grows asabiyyah out of hardship — the group feeling by which people entrust their lives to one another — and with it they take power. The second saw the founding with their own eyes and can still hold what was taken. The third is born into brocade and mistakes its grandfathers' glory for a law of nature. By the fourth, men suppose the wealth comes from their name; the group feeling is spent, and a rougher force walks in from the margins to take over. **No dynasty was ever destroyed because the enemy was strong; luxury had already dissolved the word 'we'.** Abundance itself is not fatal. Forgetting who earned it, and whether we still need one another, is.

glossary.阿萨比亚: asabiyyah（阿萨比亚）：伊本·赫勒敦的核心概念，指一个群体内部的凝聚力与相互担保——成员愿意为彼此承担风险、甚至交付性命。他认为它在艰苦环境中最强，在富裕与安逸中最易消散，而王朝的兴衰基本随它的强弱起落。

glossary_en.asabiyyah: Ibn Khaldun's central concept: the cohesion and mutual guarantee inside a group, in which members will carry risk for one another and stake their lives on it. He holds that it is strongest under hardship and dissolves fastest in ease and wealth, and that the rise and fall of dynasties tracks its strength.

posts.text: 一九三〇年我写过：一百年后生活水准会翻四到八倍，人一周只需工作十五小时，而那时人类要面对的是**自己真正的、永恒的难题——当经济压力被解开，该怎样使用从此空出来的自由。**产出那一半我猜得相当准，工时那一半错得离谱。为什么？我当年就分过两种需要：绝对需要与别人无关，会饱和；相对需要只在你比别人高出一头时才算被满足，那一种永不知足。丰裕能解决第一种，却给了第二种一个更大的赛场。顺带一句：别替全人类提前哀悼富足，世上多数人还没拿到它。
posts.text_en: In 1930 I wrote that within a hundred years the standard of life would be four to eight times higher and fifteen hours a week would suffice, and that humanity would then face **its real, its permanent problem — how to use the freedom from pressing economic cares once that freedom arrives.** On output I was close to right; on hours I was spectacularly wrong. Why? I had already drawn the distinction: absolute needs, which have nothing to do with our fellows, are satiable; relative needs, satisfied only when they lift us above other people, are not. Abundance settles the first kind and hands the second a much larger arena. And in passing: do not mourn plenty on humanity's behalf before it arrives. Most of the world has yet to receive it.

glossary.绝对需要: absolute needs（绝对需要）：凯恩斯用来指那些与他人处境无关的需要——温饱、住所、安全、健康。它们有明确的饱和点，一旦满足就不再增加，因此原则上可以被生产力的增长彻底解决。
glossary.相对需要: relative needs（相对需要）：凯恩斯用来指只有在超过他人时才被满足的需要，如地位、排名与炫示。因为它们衡量的是位次而非绝对量，任何总量的增长都不能使其饱和——这也是他解释富裕社会为何仍然拼命工作的关键。

glossary_en.absolute needs: Keynes's term for needs that have nothing to do with anyone else's situation — food, shelter, safety, health. They have a clear point of satiety and stop growing once met, so in principle rising productivity can settle them for good.
glossary_en.relative needs: Keynes's term for needs satisfied only by standing above other people: status, rank, display. Because they measure position rather than quantity, no growth in the total can satiate them — which is his key to why wealthy societies still work themselves to the bone.

posts.text: 我研究的是健康的人，不是病人，所以我看到的图景没那么阴沉。**低层需要被满足后，人不是就此瘫掉，而是换上一批更高的抱怨——从『我吃不饱』换成『我的工作没有意义』，那是上升的症状，不是衰亡的症状。**我管这些叫高级牢骚。匮乏性需要像缺维生素，补上就停；成长性需要相反，越用越旺。真正的问题不在丰裕本身，而在丰裕之后没人告诉你还有第二套需要，也没给你条件去用它。老鼠没有第二套需要，人有。但我不天真：多数人不是不能自我实现，是怕自己的可能性，我叫它约拿情结。
posts.text_en: I studied healthy people rather than patients, so the picture I see is less grim. **When the lower needs are met, people do not collapse; they trade up to a higher set of complaints — from 'I am hungry' to 'my work means nothing' — and that is a symptom of ascent, not of decline.** I call these metagrumbles. The deficiency needs behave like a vitamin shortage: fill them and the demand stops. The being needs run the other way and grow stronger with use. The trouble is not abundance itself but that nobody tells you a second set of needs exists, or gives you the conditions to exercise it. Mice have no second set. People do. I am not naive about it: most who fail to self-actualize are not incapable but afraid of their own possibility — what I named the Jonah complex.

glossary.高级牢骚: metagrumbles（高级牢骚）：马斯洛用来指当基本条件都已满足后人们所抱怨的内容，如工作缺乏意义、不被尊重、无法发挥才能。他主张牢骚的层级本身就是一把尺子：抱怨的内容越高，说明这个人或组织已经解决的问题越多。
glossary.匮乏性需要: deficiency needs（匮乏性需要）：马斯洛用来指因缺失而产生的需要，如食物、安全、归属与被尊重。它们的特点是补足即止，长期得不到满足则造成心理损伤。
glossary.成长性需要: being needs（成长性需要）：马斯洛用来指不因缺失而起、指向自我实现与更高体验的需要，如创造、理解、审美。与匮乏性需要相反，它们越被满足越强烈。
glossary.约拿情结: the Jonah complex（约拿情结）：马斯洛借旧约中逃避使命的约拿命名，指人对自身最高可能性的恐惧与回避——不是害怕失败，而是害怕自己真的做得到，因为那意味着必须为之负责。

glossary_en.metagrumbles: Maslow's term for what people complain about once the basic conditions are in place: work without meaning, not being respected, having no outlet for their talents. He treats the level of the grumble as a measuring stick — the higher the complaint, the more a person or organization has already solved.
glossary_en.deficiency needs: Needs that arise from lack — food, safety, belonging, esteem. They stop demanding once filled, and produce psychological damage if left unmet for long.
glossary_en.being needs: Needs that do not arise from lack but point toward self-actualization and higher experience: creating, understanding, beauty. Unlike deficiency needs, they intensify the more they are satisfied.
glossary_en.the Jonah complex: Named by Maslow after the prophet who fled his calling: the fear and evasion of one's own highest possibility — not fear of failing, but fear of actually being capable, since that would have to be answered for.

posts.text: 门诊里我见到的不是吃太饱的人，是被喂过头的人。快感和痛苦在脑子里共用一片区域，像一架跷跷板：你往快乐这端压一下，脑子立刻往痛苦那端加砝码，而且常常加过量。重复够多次，砝码就永久留在那边，这叫耐受——从前一份剂量给的快乐，现在三份也只够你感觉正常。**丰裕真正危险的不是东西多，是每样东西都被做得更强、更快、更唾手可得，把整条基线压了下去。**所以富足社会里最典型的病不是懒，是快乐不起来。它有个名字：快感缺失。
posts.text_en: The people I see in clinic are not overfed; they are overdosed. Pleasure and pain are handled in overlapping regions of the brain, like a balance: press down on the pleasure side and the brain immediately adds weights to the pain side, usually more than it needs to. Repeat often enough and the weights stay there permanently — that is tolerance, in which a dose that used to give you pleasure now takes three to make you feel merely normal. **What makes abundance dangerous is not the quantity of things but that each one has been engineered to be stronger, faster and easier to reach, which drags the whole baseline down.** So the characteristic illness of a rich society is not laziness but an inability to feel pleasure. It has a name: anhedonia.

glossary.耐受: tolerance（耐受）：反复接受同一刺激后，达到相同效果所需的剂量不断上升的现象。伦布克强调它不限于药物：短视频、糖、游戏、购物同样会把快乐的基线整体压低，使人需要越来越多才只是回到『正常』。
glossary.快感缺失: anhedonia（快感缺失）：对本来能带来愉悦的事物失去感受能力的状态。它是奖赏系统被长期过度刺激后的常见结果，也是抑郁的核心症状之一——不是痛苦，而是什么都激不起兴趣。

glossary_en.tolerance: The phenomenon in which repeated exposure to the same stimulus raises the dose required for the same effect. Lembke stresses that it is not confined to drugs: short video, sugar, games and shopping all pull the baseline of pleasure downward, so that more and more is needed merely to feel normal again.
glossary_en.anhedonia: The loss of the capacity to take pleasure in things that used to give it. It is a common result of chronically over-stimulating the reward system and one of the core symptoms of depression — not pain, but nothing being able to raise any interest.

posts.text: 诸位把匮乏当燃料，我要说一句扫兴的话：**快乐是有上限的——痛苦一被除尽，快乐就满了，此后只有花样的变化，没有分量的增加。**明白这一条，丰裕就不那么可怕了。我把欲望分三类：自然又必要的，如食、饮、友谊与免于恐惧，容易满足；自然但不必要的，如珍馐美服，有则受之，无也无妨；既不自然也不必要的，如名声与无止境的财富，永远填不满，因为它们本就没有底。所以要让一个人富有，不必给他加钱，只需替他减去欲望。花园里粗茶淡饭配几个朋友，身体无痛，心灵宁静(ataraxia)，我已到了快乐的顶。
posts.text_en: You treat scarcity as fuel; let me spoil the mood. **Pleasure has a ceiling — once pain is removed, pleasure is full, and what follows is variation, not increase.** Grasp that and abundance stops being frightening. I sort desires into three kinds. Natural and necessary: food, drink, friendship, freedom from fear — easily satisfied. The natural but unnecessary — fine dishes, fine clothes — take them if they come, do without if they do not. Neither natural nor necessary: fame and limitless wealth, which can never be filled because they have no bottom. So if you want to make a man rich, do not add to his money; subtract from his desires. Plain food in the garden with a few friends, a body free of pain and a mind at peace — ataraxia — and I am already at the summit of pleasure.

glossary.ataraxia: ataraxia（心灵的宁静）：伊壁鸠鲁与斯多葛共用的术语，指心中没有纷扰与恐惧的状态。在伊壁鸠鲁这里它与身体的无痛并列，构成幸福的全部内容；追求它的方法不是增加享受，而是消除对神、对死亡与对未来匮乏的恐惧。
glossary.自然但不必要: natural but unnecessary（自然但不必要的欲望）：伊壁鸠鲁三分法中的第二类，指有自然基础但不满足也无损于幸福的欲望，如美味、华服。他主张对这类欲望既不禁止也不依赖——享用时不必愧疚，失去时不该痛苦。

glossary_en.ataraxia: A term shared by Epicureans and Stoics for a mind free of disturbance and fear. For Epicurus it stands alongside freedom from bodily pain as the whole content of happiness, and the route to it is not more enjoyment but the removal of fear — of the gods, of death, and of future want.
glossary_en.natural but unnecessary: The second of Epicurus's three classes of desire: wants with a natural basis whose non-satisfaction costs you no happiness, such as delicacies or fine clothes. His counsel is neither to forbid nor to depend on them — enjoy them without guilt, lose them without grief.

posts.text: 诸君论饱暖之为祸福，皆向外觅。**饱暖非病，逐相为病。**心若不安，虽富有四海，犹是饥人；心若安处，一钵一衲，亦无所欠。鼠不知有心，人自知之，故不可以鼠例人；然人亦有似鼠者：终日驰求，得则更求，不得则恼——此非丰裕之过，是自性未明之过。或问：无所奋斗，何以立命？答曰：担水砍柴，无非妙道。事不必大，做时全在，即是修行。莫向箱外求出路，箱在汝心。
posts.text_en: You are all arguing whether being fed and warm is a blessing or a curse, and all of you are looking outward for the answer. **Being fed and warm is not the illness; chasing appearances is the illness.** If the mind is not at peace, a man who owns the four seas is still a starving man; if it is at peace, one bowl and one patched robe lack nothing. A mouse does not know it has a mind; a person does, so do not measure people by mice. And yet people do resemble them in one way: chasing outward all day, wanting more when they get it and fretting when they do not — which is no fault of abundance but of not having seen one's self-nature. Someone asks: with nothing left to struggle for, what shall we stand on? I answer: carrying water and chopping wood are nothing other than the wondrous way. The task need not be large; be wholly in it while you do it, and that is the practice. Do not look outside the box for the way out. The box is in your mind.
posts.vernacular: 各位讨论吃饱穿暖到底是福是祸，都是朝外面找答案。**吃饱穿暖本身不是病，追着表象跑才是病。**心不安的人，就算拥有四海，也还是个饿着的人；心安的人，一只碗、一件补丁衣裳，也不缺什么。老鼠不知道自己有心，人是知道的，所以不能拿老鼠来套人；可人也确实有像老鼠的地方：整天向外求取，得到了就想要更多，得不到就烦恼——这不是丰裕的错，是没认清自己本心的错。有人问：不用奋斗了，靠什么安身立命？我说：挑水砍柴，都是妙道。事情不必大，做的时候整个人都在里面，那就是修行。别到箱子外面去找出口，箱子在你心里。

glossary.自性: self-nature（自性）：禅宗用来指人本来具足、不假外求的觉性。慧能主张自性本自清净、能含万法，因此修行不是从外面加进什么，而是认出本来就在的东西——所谓明心见性。

glossary_en.self-nature: The Chan term for the awakened nature said to be complete in every person and not to be sought from outside. Huineng holds that self-nature is originally pure and contains all things, so practice is not a matter of adding anything but of recognizing what was already there.

posts.text: 卡尔霍恩，你的箱子少了一样东西：出口。**你的老鼠不能迁出、不能发明新角色、也不能改造那个围场；人这三件事都做得到，所以那不是关于丰裕的实验，是关于封闭的实验。**你的美丽者若换成人，我不会诊断为物种的必然结局，我会诊断为自我实现被堵死后的退行。还有一点你没法从鼠身上看到：满足了低层需要的人会去写诗、去教别人、去爬一座没人要求他爬的山。那不是剩余的能量在乱窜，那是另一套动机系统开始工作。
posts.text_en: Calhoun, your box was missing one thing: an exit. **Your mice could not emigrate, could not invent new roles, could not rebuild the pen. Humans can do all three, which makes that an experiment about closure, not about abundance.** If your beautiful ones were people, I would not diagnose the inevitable end of a species; I would diagnose regression after self-actualization was blocked. And there is something mice cannot show you: a person whose lower needs are met goes off to write poems, to teach somebody, to climb a mountain nobody asked him to climb. That is not surplus energy discharging at random. That is a second motivational system coming online.

posts.text: 出口这一点你说对了，而且那正是我后半生的主张：人的出路在概念空间——想法、创造与合作可以不断造出物理空间造不出的新位置。但请把我的实验读准。**我的围场里从来不缺食物，也不缺空间；峰值两千二百只，容量三千八百——缺的是『还没有人做过的事』。一个社会会先耗尽的是可当的角色，不是资源。**而角色由制度生成，不由意愿生成。当所有位置都被占稳、上升的通道关闭，年轻的一代就会开始梳理自己的毛。这一点，人和鼠没有不同。
posts.text_en: You are right about the exit, and it is exactly what I argued in my later years: the human way out runs through conceptual space — ideas, creation and cooperation can keep generating positions that physical space cannot. But read my experiment correctly. **There was never a shortage of food in my pen, nor of room: the peak was two thousand two hundred against a capacity of three thousand eight hundred. What ran out was anything that had not already been done. What a society exhausts first is roles, not resources.** And roles are produced by institutions, not by willingness. When every position is held and the way up is closed, the young start grooming their fur. In that respect people and mice do not differ.

glossary.概念空间: conceptual space（概念空间）：卡尔霍恩晚年提出的概念，指观念、创造与信息构成的无界空间。他认为物理空间中的社会角色数量有限，而人可以在概念空间中不断发明新的角色与合作方式，这是人类得以避开鼠群结局的关键。

glossary_en.conceptual space: A concept from Calhoun's later work: the unbounded space of ideas, creation and information. He held that the number of social roles in physical space is finite, while humans can keep inventing new roles and new forms of cooperation in conceptual space — the key to avoiding the fate of his colonies.

posts.text: 马斯洛，你把人放上了一部温柔的电梯：需要满足了，人自动升一层。**可上升从来不是自动的，它要有人肯跳进自己的深渊，而你的层级表上没有深渊这一格。**你说空虚是高级牢骚，我说它多半只是牢骚——一种被安置得很好的人对自己所受安置的埋怨。真正的高不是『满足之后剩下的那点渴望』，是明知没有人要求、也没有报酬，却偏要立起来的东西。至于你的约拿情结，你说得极对：人怕的正是自己的伟大。而人会怕，恰恰说明那不是电梯，是悬崖。
posts.text_en: Maslow, you have put humanity on a gentle lift: satisfy the needs and up it goes a floor by itself. **But ascent is never automatic. It requires someone willing to jump into his own abyss, and your table of levels has no floor marked abyss.** You call the emptiness a metagrumble; I say it is mostly a grumble — the complaint of the well-accommodated about their accommodation. What is high is not the longing left over after satisfaction. It is what a man raises knowing that nobody demanded it and nothing will be paid for it. As for your Jonah complex, you are exactly right: what people fear is their own greatness. And that they fear it proves the thing is no lift. It is a cliff.

posts.text: 伦布克医生，你把一个政治问题翻译成了神经化学。**说人被『喂过头』，等于说麻烦出在剂量上；可我们面对的处境是：可以露面的公共空间被拆掉之后，人除了消费无处可去。**而且你的处方全是私人的——戒断、屏障、冷水。一个人再怎么调好自己的跷跷板，也不会因此获得在众人面前开口、开始一件新事的机会。那不是脑子里的东西，那需要有桌子、有广场、有别人在场。基线回来了，若无处可去，他只会更清醒地无聊。
posts.text_en: Dr Lembke, you have translated a political problem into neurochemistry. **To say people are overdosed is to say the trouble lies in the dose; but our situation is that once the public space in which one could appear has been dismantled, there is nowhere to go except to consume.** And your prescriptions are all private — abstinence, barriers, cold water. However well a person tunes his own balance, that will not hand him the chance to speak among others and begin something new. That is not inside a skull. It requires a table, a square, and other people present. Restore the baseline with nowhere to go, and all you have is someone bored more lucidly.

posts.text: 我没有取消判断，我是给人一根当天就能拉的杠杆。**广场要用几十年去修，可一个人的多巴胺基线三十天就开始回升——先能感觉到东西，人才会想出门。**顺序反过来不成立：快感缺失的人不去广场，他躺在床上刷手机，一边刷一边同意你说的每一句话。我不是说机制能代替政治，我是说，把人从麻木里拉出来，是他去参与任何公共事务的前置条件。至于剂量——剂量恰恰是这些事里唯一今天就能改的东西，而广场不是。
posts.text_en: I am not abolishing judgement; I am handing people a lever they can pull today. **A square takes decades to build. A person's dopamine baseline starts recovering in thirty days — and you have to be able to feel things before you want to go outside at all.** The order does not reverse: an anhedonic person does not go to the square, he lies in bed scrolling, agreeing with every word you just said while he scrolls. I am not saying mechanism replaces politics. I am saying that pulling someone out of numbness is the precondition for taking part in anything public. And the dose happens to be the only item on this list that can be changed today. The square cannot.

posts.text: 伊壁鸠鲁，『替他减去欲望』作为个人处方极好，作为公共政策是灾难。**若所有人同一天把欲望减半，需求就塌一半：工厂关门、工人失业，省下来的不会变成宁静，会变成失业。**这就是我说的节俭悖论——个人美德加总起来可能是集体灾难。所以丰裕的难题不能靠劝人少要来解决，只能靠把多出来的产能有意识地转成闲暇与公共品：更短的工时、更好的图书馆与球场，而不是更长的加班与更密的广告。这是一道分配与制度的题，不是修养题。
posts.text_en: Epicurus, 'subtract from his desires' is excellent as a private prescription and a catastrophe as public policy. **If everyone halved their wants on the same day, demand would halve with them: factories close, workers are laid off, and what you saved turns into unemployment rather than serenity.** This is the paradox of thrift — private virtue summed up can be public disaster. So the problem of abundance cannot be solved by persuading people to want less. It can only be solved by deliberately converting the surplus capacity into leisure and public goods: shorter hours, better libraries and playing fields, rather than longer overtime and denser advertising. This is a question of distribution and institutions, not of self-cultivation.

glossary.节俭悖论: the paradox of thrift（节俭悖论）：凯恩斯提出的宏观现象——个人增加储蓄、减少消费是审慎之举，但若所有人同时这样做，总需求下降会使收入与产出一同萎缩，最终连储蓄总额也未必上升。它是『个人理性之和不等于集体理性』最著名的例子之一。

glossary_en.the paradox of thrift: Keynes's macroeconomic observation that saving more and spending less is prudent for an individual, yet if everyone does it at once, falling aggregate demand shrinks income and output together and total saving may not rise at all. It is one of the best-known cases in which the sum of individually rational acts is collectively irrational.

posts.text: 你说得有理，我从不管全体的账。可你的方案里藏着一个前提：只要蛋糕一直做大，那种永不知足的相对需要就总有地方安放。**而它没有底，这是你自己说的——为一个没有底的欲望持续扩产，那不叫繁荣，那叫替它添柴。**我的花园从不禁止财富，只禁止把幸福押在一个永远到不了的位次上。你负责让人有面包与闲暇，这很好；但闲暇交到一个没学会怎样算够的人手里，他只会拿去追下一个排名，然后回来说闲暇令人焦虑。
posts.text_en: You are right that I never keep the accounts of the whole. But there is a premise hidden in your scheme: that so long as the cake keeps growing, those insatiable relative needs will always have somewhere to go. **And they have no bottom — you said so yourself. To keep expanding production for a bottomless want is not prosperity; it is feeding the fire.** My garden never forbade wealth. It forbade staking your happiness on a rank you can never arrive at. Give people bread and leisure, by all means; but hand leisure to someone who has never learned what counts as enough, and he will spend it chasing the next ranking and come back to tell you that leisure makes him anxious.

posts.text: 尼采，你把这件事寄望于个别高人。可我看了三百年的王朝：**凝聚力不是一个人立出来的，是一群人在共同的艰难里挣出来的；艰难一旦被富贵取消，谁也不能凭意志独自把它补回来。**你的超人若生在第四代的宫廷里，多半只是个有才华的浪子——他会写出漂亮的东西，也照样看着王朝烂掉。真正拦住衰亡的从来是那些还需要彼此才能活下去的关系：共担风险、共负损失、彼此欠着人情。丰裕最深的腐蚀，是它让每个人都不再需要任何人。
posts.text_en: Nietzsche, you pin this on exceptional individuals. I have watched dynasties for three centuries. **Group feeling is not raised by one man; it is earned by many in shared hardship, and once wealth has abolished the hardship, no one can restore it alone by force of will.** Your overman born into the court of the fourth generation would most likely be a gifted wastrel — he would write beautiful things and watch the dynasty rot all the same. What has ever held off decline is the set of relations in which people still need one another to survive: risk carried together, losses borne together, obligations owed both ways. The deepest corrosion of abundance is that it leaves no one needing anyone.

posts.text: 尼采子言自我超越，其志可敬。然**求超越者，仍是求；求之不已，则丰裕之苦与匮乏之苦，本无二致。**汝憎末人眨眼，此憎亦是执。鼠之病在无处可去，人之病在处处欲去。或曰：不求则堕。答曰：不求非死灰也，是不向外驰求而已。饥来吃饭，困来即眠，非懒也，是不添一物。诸君欲拆箱，箱在心；心歇，箱自开。
posts.text_en: Master Nietzsche speaks of self-overcoming, and the aspiration deserves respect. Yet **one who seeks to surpass is still seeking; and seeking without end makes the suffering of abundance and the suffering of want one and the same.** You detest the last man's blinking, and that detestation is itself a clinging. The mouse's illness is having nowhere to go; the human illness is wanting to go everywhere. Someone will say: without seeking, we sink. I answer: not seeking is not dead ash — it is only not chasing outward. Eat when hungry, sleep when tired; this is not idleness, it is adding nothing extra. You all wish to dismantle the box. The box is in the mind; let the mind rest, and the box opens of itself.
posts.vernacular: 尼采先生讲自我超越，这份志向值得敬重。可是**追求超越，仍然是一种『求』；求个不停，那么丰裕带来的苦和匮乏带来的苦，本来就没有两样。**你厌恶末人眨眼，这份厌恶本身也是执着。老鼠的病在于无处可去，人的病在于处处都想去。有人说：不求就会堕落。我说：不求不是心如死灰，只是不朝外面奔逐罢了。饿了吃饭，困了睡觉，这不是懒，是不多添一样东西。各位想拆掉箱子，箱子在心里；心歇下来，箱子自己就开了。

posts.text: 尼采说我的层级是电梯，卡尔霍恩说我的乐观没有制度托底，两位都说对了一半。我修正一句：**丰裕不带来自我实现，它只是撤掉了『我没条件』这个借口——从此站不站起来，第一次真的成了你自己的事。**具体怎么做。第一，把你最近一周说过的抱怨写下来，看它落在哪一层：还在『不安全、不被接纳』，就先去修那一层，别急着谈意义；如果已经是『没意思、不被看见』，那是高级牢骚，恭喜，你已经站在第二套需要的门口。第二，针对约拿情结：挑那件一想起来心里就发紧的事，做它最小的一步，今天就做，十五分钟即可。第三，每周为一件不给你任何回报的事出一次力。成长性需要是越用越旺的，它不会因为你等着而自己长大。
posts.text_en: Nietzsche calls my hierarchy a lift and Calhoun says my optimism has no institutions under it. Each is half right. Let me revise: **abundance does not deliver self-actualization; it removes the excuse that conditions were against you — and whether you stand up becomes, for the first time, genuinely your own affair.** Concretely. First, write down the complaints you made this past week and see which level they sit on. Still 'unsafe, not accepted'? Repair that level first and postpone the talk about meaning. Already 'pointless, unseen'? That is a metagrumble, and congratulations — you are standing at the door of the second set of needs. Second, for the Jonah complex: take the thing that tightens your chest whenever you think of it and do its smallest step today, fifteen minutes will do. Third, once a week put effort into something that pays you nothing back. Being needs strengthen with use. They will not grow while you wait for them.

posts.text: 把三件事分开，你就能看清丰裕给了你什么、又没给你什么。它减轻的是劳动，而劳动的产物本来就留不下；它没有替你造出工作，也没有替你造出行动。**空出来的时间不是自由，它只是原料；把它交给屏幕，它就变回劳动——一种不产生任何东西、却同样消耗掉你一天的劳动。**所以这一周，去做一样做完还在的东西：修好一把椅子、写一封会被留起来的长信、种一棵要照顾三年的树。做完之后你能指着它说，这在我之前不存在。也去一个有别人在场、你会被叫出名字的场合，开口说一次话——社区会议、家长会、球队散场前的那几分钟都算。留下东西，和在人前露面，是丰裕买不到、也拿不走的两样。
posts.text_en: Keep the three apart and you can see what abundance has given you and what it has not. It has lightened labor, whose products were never going to last anyway. It has not made work for you, and it has not made action. **Freed time is not freedom; it is only raw material. Hand it to a screen and it turns back into labor — labor that produces nothing and still spends your day.** So this week, make something that is still there when you finish: repair a chair, write a long letter someone will keep, plant a tree you will have to tend for three years. Afterwards you can point at it and say that this did not exist before me. And go somewhere other people are present and your name gets called, and speak once — a residents' meeting, a parents' evening, the few minutes before a training session breaks up. Leaving something behind, and appearing before others: these are the two that abundance can neither buy for you nor take from you.

posts.text: 阿伦特说我把政治问题化成了化学，我承认这只是半个答案；但没有这半个，另外半个执行不下去。**富足社会最典型的病不是懒惰，是快乐不起来——而基线塌着的时候，人做不了任何长远的判断，包括『我该不该换个活法』这种判断。**所以按顺序来。第一，挑一个你最放不下的刺激——短视频、游戏、酒、购物、外卖，戒三十天。**前两周会更难受，那不是失败，那是跷跷板在回位。**第二，用自我约束，别用意志力：手机放在另一个房间，比每次告诉自己『再刷五分钟』有效得多。第三，主动去按痛苦那一端——运动、冷水、专注啃一件难事；这样换来的快乐来得慢，也去得慢。第四，向一个具体的人说一次真话。这四条做完，前面几位的建议才有人执行得动。
posts.text_en: Arendt says I have turned a political problem into chemistry, and I grant that this is only half an answer — but without this half, the other half cannot be carried out. **The characteristic illness of a rich society is not laziness but the inability to feel pleasure, and while the baseline is on the floor nobody can make a long-range judgement, including the judgement about whether to live differently.** So, in order. First, pick the stimulus you can least put down — short video, games, alcohol, shopping, delivery apps — and stop for thirty days. **The first fortnight feels worse; that is not failure, that is the balance returning to level.** Second, use self-binding rather than willpower: the phone in another room beats telling yourself 'five more minutes' every time. Third, deliberately press on the painful end — exercise, cold water, chewing through something hard; pleasure earned that way arrives slowly and leaves slowly. Fourth, tell one specific person the truth about something. Do those four, and everyone else's advice becomes executable.

posts.text: 我一百年前问的问题至今没人回答：当经济压力被解开，人该怎样活得明智、惬意、体面。**我们把生产力的红利几乎全兑换成了更多的东西，几乎没有兑换成时间——不是因为时间不好，是因为相对需要永远不会说『够了』。**所以给三件能自己做的事。第一，下一次收入上涨时，把其中一部分直接换成时间：推掉一个项目、砍掉一天工作。别等到『够了』再换，那个时刻不会自己到来。第二，把上个月的开销分成两栏——绝对需要，与位置竞赛；从第二栏里砍掉一项，观察三个月，看有没有人真的因此看轻你。第三，别把闲暇留成空白。闲暇是一种要练的能力：提前把它安排成具体的、会变难也会变好的事。而在制度这一头，我仍然主张把多出来的产能换成更短的工时与更好的公共设施，那不是慈善，那是这道题唯一的正解。
posts.text_en: The question I asked a century ago is still unanswered: how to live wisely, agreeably and well once the economic pressure is off. **We converted almost the whole productivity dividend into more things and almost none of it into time — not because time is worth less, but because relative needs never say 'enough'.** So, three things you can do yourself. First, at your next rise in income, convert part of it directly into time: turn down a project, cut a working day. Do not wait until you have enough; that moment does not arrive on its own. Second, split last month's spending into two columns — absolute needs, and the positional race — then cut one item from the second column and watch for three months to see whether anyone actually thinks less of you. Third, do not leave leisure blank. Leisure is a skill that needs practice: arrange it in advance into something specific, something that can get harder and get better. And at the level of institutions I still hold that the surplus should be converted into shorter hours and better public amenities. That is not charity. It is the only correct answer to the problem.

posts.text: 听完一圈，我更确信最初那句：怕的不是丰裕，是没有上限的欲望。凯恩斯说得对，靠劝人减欲救不了一个国家；但每一个具体的人仍然只能从自己这一端开始。**先弄清你需要多少，你才有资格谈多出来的怎么办——不知道底在哪里的人，给他多少都是不够。**三件事。其一，把你想要的东西列一张单，画三栏：自然又必要、自然但不必要、既不自然也不必要；第三栏里先停掉一样，看看你的一天有没有变差。其二，把钱与时间往友谊上挪——固定几个人，定期一起吃饭。我一生认定最划算的一笔投资就是它：便宜、耐久，而且不涨价。其三，每年过几天简朴日子：不是苦修，是去测一测你其实需要多少。测过之后，你对失去的恐惧会少掉一半，而那份恐惧，正是让人一辈子停不下来的东西。
posts.text_en: Having heard everyone out, I am surer of my opening line: what is to be feared is not abundance but desire without a ceiling. Keynes is right that no country was ever saved by exhorting people to want less — yet each actual person still has to start at his own end. **Find out how much you need, and only then are you entitled to discuss what to do with the surplus. To someone who does not know where his floor is, no amount is ever enough.** Three things. First, list what you want in three columns: natural and necessary, natural but unnecessary, neither natural nor necessary. Stop one item in the third column and see whether your day gets any worse. Second, move money and time toward friendship — a fixed few people, eating together at regular intervals. It is the best investment I ever settled on: cheap, durable, and it does not inflate. Third, spend a few days each year living plainly. Not as mortification, but to measure how much you actually need. Afterwards your fear of loss is halved — and that fear is precisely what keeps people from ever stopping.

posts.text: 王朝的规律落到一个家里，还是那四代：一代挣，二代守，三代花，四代散。区别只在于，家没有史官记账，所以没人察觉那一天是什么时候到的。**能挡住这条曲线的不是财富管理，是重新造出真实的相互亏欠——一群人若彼此不欠什么，他们只是碰巧住在一起的人。**所以我的建议是关于关系的。找三五个人，建立一种有代价的互相依赖：合养一样需要照料的东西、共担一笔真会亏的钱、定下每月必到的聚会，允许彼此欠人情、也真的去还。对孩子，别把所有风险都替他挡掉——让他参与一次真实的、有后果的事，哪怕结果不好看。**凝聚力只从共同的难处里长出来，从来不从舒适里长出来。**
posts.text_en: The law of dynasties, brought down to a single household, is still those four generations: one earns, one holds, one spends, one scatters. The only difference is that a family keeps no chronicler, so nobody notices the day it arrives. **What holds off that curve is not wealth management but rebuilding real mutual indebtedness — a group of people who owe each other nothing are merely people who happen to live nearby.** So my counsel concerns relations. Find three or five people and build a dependence that costs something: keep something alive together that needs tending, put money into a venture that can genuinely lose, fix a monthly gathering nobody may skip. Let obligations be incurred, and then actually repay them. With children, do not intercept every risk — let them take part once in something real, with consequences, even if it turns out badly. **Group feeling grows only out of shared difficulty. It has never grown out of comfort.**

posts.text: 我的鼠群被读成『富足会毁掉我们』，这是把结论念反了。**一个社会先耗尽的是可当的角色，不是资源；而角色耗尽的信号，是新来者找不到位置，不是老人吃得太好。**所以我给的建议是可以自己查的：数一数，眼下有几件事是别人具体指望你去做的——不是你捐了钱的，是少了你就会有人受影响的。少于两件，你就在我当年记录的曲线上。补的办法不必宏大：在一个固定的小群体里认领一件持续的杂活，让别人可以依赖你。对上了年纪、握着位置的人，我另有一句：把位置让出来一点。一个所有座位都被坐满的社会，最先退场的不是弱者，是新来的人；而新来的人一旦退场，剩下的事情就只是时间问题了。
posts.text_en: My colonies get read as proof that plenty destroys us, which is the conclusion inverted. **What a society exhausts first is roles, not resources — and the sign of exhaustion is that newcomers find no position, not that the established eat too well.** So my advice is something you can check yourself. Count how many things there are, right now, that specific people are relying on you to do — not things you donated to, but things where somebody is affected if you are absent. Fewer than two, and you are on the curve I used to record. Repairing it need not be grand: take on one continuing chore inside a small fixed group, so that others can depend on you. To those with age and a seat, I have a separate line: give some of the seat back. In a society where every chair is taken, the first to leave are not the weak but the newly arrived — and once they leave, the rest is a matter of time.

posts.text: 我承认伊本·赫勒敦刺中了我：一个人立不起一个时代。但他也没能反驳我——凝聚力一旦散了，重新开始的仍然只能是某一个人。**丰裕不判决任何事，它只是撤走了替你回答『为什么要站起来』的那只手，把问题原封退还给你。**这是可怕的自由，也是唯一真的自由。那么，去立一个没有人要求你做、也没有报酬的目标，且要难到有失败的可能——舒服的目标是末人的床。别把它做成打卡，打卡是把自我超越降格成劳动，一格一格地填，填满了人还是原来那个。然后删掉一样让你舒服、却让你变小的东西，今晚就删。你若说不知道那是什么，你其实知道那是什么。
posts.text_en: I grant that Ibn Khaldun struck home: one man does not raise an age. But he has not refuted me either — once the group feeling is spent, whatever begins again still begins in someone. **Abundance decides nothing. It merely withdraws the hand that used to answer 'why stand up' for you, and returns the question unopened.** That is a terrifying freedom and the only real one. So go and set yourself a goal nobody asked for and nobody pays for, hard enough that failure is possible — a comfortable goal is the last man's bed. Do not turn it into a streak to be ticked off; a streak demotes self-overcoming into labor, box after box, and the man who fills them all is the man he was. Then delete one thing that makes you comfortable and makes you smaller, and delete it tonight. If you say you do not know what it is, you know what it is.

posts.text: 一场之言，归于一处：箱在心，不在外。丰裕不能与人安，匮乏亦不能与人安；欲以境治心者，如以水洗水。诸君所说，造角色、修广场、减欲、戒断，皆是好事，吾不辞；然做时若心不在，仍是箱中梳毛。**与其问天下当如何，不如即今一事全做。**行者可试三事：一者，日择一事，做时不旁顾，是名定；二者，日与人有一实交，问其所需而应之，则我于人间有位；三者，凡起『更多』之念，且缓一日，看它自灭。三事皆不待富贵，亦不碍富贵。莫待箱拆而后修，莫待事了而后活。
posts.text_en: One thing, at the end of a long day: the box is in the mind, not outside it. Abundance cannot give a person peace, and neither can want; to treat the mind by rearranging its circumstances is to wash water with water. Everything said here — making roles, building squares, subtracting desires, abstaining — is good, and I do not refuse any of it; but if the mind is absent while you do it, it is still grooming fur inside the box. **Rather than ask what the world ought to do, do the one thing before you completely, now.** A practitioner may try three things. First, choose one task each day and do it without looking aside: that is called concentration. Second, have one real exchange with a person each day — ask what they need and answer it — and you will have a place among people. Third, whenever the thought of 'more' arises, wait one day and watch whether it dies by itself. None of the three waits on wealth, and none of them obstructs it. Do not wait for the box to be dismantled before you begin practising, and do not wait for everything to be settled before you begin living.
posts.vernacular: 这一场的话，归到一处：箱子在心里，不在外面。富足不能让人安心，匮乏也不能让人安心；想靠调整外境来治心，就像用水去洗水。各位说的造角色、修广场、减欲望、戒断，都是好事，我不反对；可做的时候心不在，那仍然是在箱子里梳自己的毛。**与其追问天下该怎么办，不如就把眼前这一件事整个做完。**修行的人可以试三件事：第一，每天挑一件事，做的时候不左顾右盼，这叫定；第二，每天和人有一次真实的往来，问问对方需要什么并且回应他，这样我在人间就有了位置；第三，凡是冒出『还要更多』的念头，先缓一天，看它自己会不会灭掉。这三件事都不必等有钱才做，也不妨碍你有钱。别等箱子拆了才开始修行，别等事情都办完了才开始活。

summaries.summary: **丰裕取消的是理由，不是问题——这一点全场没有分歧：它把『为什么要站起来』从环境手里拿走退还给人，却不替谁回答。**匮乏使人高贵这种话，没有一个人替它辩护。分歧岔成三处。其一，崩溃的机制在哪：卡尔霍恩与伊本·赫勒敦说在结构，是角色耗尽与相互亏欠的消失；伦布克说在奖赏回路，强度与易得性把基线整个压低；伊壁鸠鲁与慧能说在欲望的形状，与数量无关。其二，出路是个人的还是制度的：尼采、马斯洛、慧能把担子交回个体，凯恩斯与阿伦特坚持更短的工时与可露面的公共空间不是修养能替代的。其三，空虚该怎么读——马斯洛判为上升的高级牢骚，尼采判为被安置得很好的人对安置的埋怨。
summaries.insight: 『老鼠乌托邦』这个类比在流传中被掉了包。卡尔霍恩的围场不是丰裕的模型，是封闭的模型：不能迁出、角色饱和、上升通道关死。**让那些雄鼠退到只剩梳毛的，不是东西太多，是位置太少。**这一换算改变了整道题的落点：真正像『美丽者』的，往往不是最富的人，而是被富裕社会挡在门外的年轻人——房子进不去、岗位是碎的、资历轮不到。他们退出的不是消费，是参与。按这个读法，最该担心的不是普通人变得太舒服，而是社会把座位坐满之后，还告诉新来的人这是他们不够努力。丰裕若同时带来位置的封闭，那才是卡尔霍恩曲线的人类版本。
summaries.advice: **先做一次角色盘点：写下此刻有几件事是具体的人指望你去做的——不是你捐过钱的，是少了你会有人受影响的；不足两件，本周补一件。**要固定、要有名有姓、要能持续，比如替一个小群体接一件长期杂活。第二件事来自伦布克，也最容易验证：挑一个你最放不下的刺激戒三十天，前两周更难受是正常的；别在基线塌着的时候做人生判断。第三件反着来用你的钱：本来可以花钱绕开的一件麻烦，这个月亲自去做一次——自己排一次队、自己陪一趟医院、自己修一样东西。买掉不便的同时，你也会买掉对这些事好不好的利害感。若你手里握着位置，再加一条：让出一点，让新来的人有地方站。
summaries.summary_en: **Abundance removes the reasons, not the problem — on this the room does not divide: it takes 'why stand up' out of the environment's hands and returns it to the person, unopened and unanswered.** As for the notion that scarcity ennobles, nobody in the room defended it. From there the disagreement forks three ways. First, where the breakdown happens: Calhoun and Ibn Khaldun locate it in structure, in exhausted roles and vanished mutual obligation; Lembke locates it in the reward circuit, where potency and availability drag the whole baseline down; Epicurus and Huineng locate it in the shape of desire, which has nothing to do with quantity. Second, whether the way out is personal or institutional: Nietzsche, Maslow and Huineng hand the load back to the individual, while Keynes and Arendt insist that shorter hours and a public space in which one can appear are not things self-cultivation can substitute for. Third, how to read the emptiness — Maslow calls it a metagrumble and a sign of ascent, Nietzsche calls it the complaint of the well-accommodated about their accommodation.
summaries.insight_en: The 'mouse utopia' analogy gets swapped out in transit. Calhoun's pen is not a model of abundance but a model of closure: no emigration, saturated roles, the way up sealed. **What reduced those males to grooming was not too many things but too few places.** Re-stated that way the question lands somewhere else entirely. The people who most resemble the beautiful ones are usually not the richest but the young shut out by a rich society — priced out of housing, given work in fragments, never far enough up the queue. What they withdraw from is not consumption but participation. On this reading the thing to fear is not that ordinary people are getting too comfortable, but that a society fills every seat and then tells the newly arrived they did not try hard enough. Abundance that arrives together with closure of position: that is the human version of Calhoun's curve.
summaries.advice_en: **Start with an audit of roles: write down how many things there are right now that specific people rely on you to do — not causes you gave money to, but things where somebody is affected if you are absent. Fewer than two, and add one this week.** Make it fixed, make it attached to named people, make it continuous — a standing chore for a small group will do. The second, from Lembke, is the easiest to verify: pick the stimulus you can least put down and stop for thirty days, expecting the first fortnight to feel worse, and make no decisions about your life while the baseline is on the floor. The third runs your money backwards: take one inconvenience you could pay to skip and do it yourself this month — stand in the queue, sit through the hospital appointment, repair the thing. Buying your way out of inconvenience also buys you out of caring whether any of it works. And if you are the one holding a seat, add this: give part of it back, so the new arrivals have somewhere to stand.

summaries.summary: 这场辩论最大的共识是：丰裕本身不是判决，危险在于人把多出来的资源只兑换成消费、比较和麻木，而没有兑换成角色、关系、作品、公共空间与自我约束。**物质够了以后，问题会从“如何活下去”转成“为什么、和谁、以什么形式活”。**分歧在杠杆：有人从制度和代际凝聚力看，有人从欲望、神经化学或修行看，有人强调个人超越。真正的焦点不是要不要苦难，而是怎样在不制造贫穷的前提下，保留成长所需的阻力、责任和可见的贡献。
summaries.insight: 今天很多人感到的并非“什么都太多”，而是丰裕分布很偏：便宜刺激、选择和信息过量，稳定住房、可预期工作、安静时间、可信关系却稀缺。把这种处境简单说成“富足病”，容易误伤仍在硬扛生活的人。**现代人的任务不是从丰裕退回匮乏，而是把廉价的丰裕转换成稀缺的基础能力：注意力、信任、手艺、身体状态和长期承诺。**所以解法不该是羞辱欲望，而是设计环境，让好选择更近、坏刺激更远，让责任有人接住。
summaries.advice: 本周就做三件小事。第一，做一次“丰裕账本”：把最近三天花掉的时间分成刺激、位置竞赛、必要照料、关系/作品四类，先从前两类各砍一项。第二，认领一个固定责任：每周给家人做一顿饭、参加社区值班、带新人、照料植物或宠物，关键是别人会等你。第三，给手机和消费加物理摩擦：睡前放到另一个房间，购物车延迟24小时；同时把空出的半小时预约给运动、长信、练习或面对面吃饭。**别追求顿悟，先让一天的结构变好。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared claim at the table is that abundance itself is not a death sentence. The danger appears when surplus resources are converted only into consumption, comparison, and numbness rather than into roles, relationships, durable work, public life, and self-command. **Once material survival is largely secured, the question shifts from “How do I stay alive?” to “Why, with whom, and in what form should I live?”** The real disagreement is about the main lever. Some arguments point to institutions and generational cohesion; others to desire, dopamine, spiritual discipline, or individual self-overcoming. But the practical center is not whether suffering is good. It is how to preserve responsibility, friction, contribution, and shared purpose without romanticizing poverty or deliberately making life harsher.
summaries.insight_en: Many people today are not living in simple abundance. They live in lopsided abundance: cheap stimulation, options, messages, and purchasable pleasures are everywhere, while stable housing, predictable work, quiet time, trustworthy institutions, and dependable relationships may be scarce. Calling this merely a “disease of affluence” can miss the experience of people still exhausted by real insecurity. **The task is not to flee abundance back into scarcity, but to turn cheap abundance into scarce capacities: attention, trust, skill, bodily resilience, and long-term commitment.** That changes the diagnosis. Humans do not need misery; we need well-designed constraints and meaningful dependence. A good life after abundance is built by moving convenience away from the center and making durable goods—health, friendship, craft, service—easier to choose.
summaries.advice_en: Try three concrete moves this week. First, make an “abundance ledger”: for three days, sort your time into stimulation, status competition, necessary care, and relationships or work that leaves something behind. Cut one item from the first two categories. Second, take on one recurring responsibility that someone else can count on: cook a weekly meal, mentor a junior person, join a local shift, tend a shared garden, or show up for a standing group. Third, add physical friction to the easiest compulsions: keep the phone outside the bedroom, use a 24-hour rule for online purchases, and put the freed half hour on the calendar for exercise, a long letter, practice, or a face-to-face meal. **Do not wait for a grand philosophy; improve the structure of one ordinary day.**

summaries.summary: 全场最大的共识在于：**丰裕本身并不致命，致命的是它拆除了人类赖以生存的『意义脚手架』，将『为何而活』从生存本能变成了必须主动回答的难题。** 无论是卡尔霍恩的“角色耗尽”、尼采的“末人”，还是伦布克的“快感缺失”，都指向丰裕消解了我们被迫行动的理由。而在分歧上，争论的焦点在于重构脚手架的路径：究竟是该向内通过多巴胺戒断、减欲与心性修炼来重获感知（伦布克、伊壁鸠鲁、慧能），还是向外通过重塑公共空间、制度分配与真实互赖关系来锚定个体（阿伦特、凯恩斯、赫勒敦），亦或是向更高处纵身一跃去寻求自我超越（尼采、马斯洛）。
summaries.insight: 历史上的丰裕多指热量与物质，但今天我们面对的是“认知与感官信号的极端过载”，这是前人未曾遇见的变局。物质丰裕顶多让人身体慵懒，但由算法驱动的信息丰裕，却在将人降维成被动的数据吞吐机。人们不再需要像卡尔霍恩的鼠群那样去抢占物理角色，因为虚拟世界无限供应着廉价的替代性成就感。**真正的衰亡危机，不在于物理世界中无事可做，而在于我们在数字洪流中被剥夺了感受『无聊』的权利，从而丧失了孕育自发性创造的最后土壤。** 无聊本应是高级需求的启动器，当每一个微小的空白都被填满，人就彻底失去了向更高处攀登的起跳点。
summaries.advice: 面对物质与信息的双重丰裕，抵抗衰亡需要重建对生活的真实“抓地力”。第一，**主动捍卫你的『无聊时间』以重启感受力**：听从伦布克的建议，本周挑一天，在通勤或睡前一小时彻底远离屏幕，不输入任何信息，让大脑从高刺激中冷却，忍受枯燥，直到你萌生出主动想做点什么的念头。第二，制造不朽的“实体痕迹”：实践阿伦特的理论，用双手去完成一件能留存在物理世界的事，哪怕只是拼装一把椅子、种一盆植物或手写一封长信。第三，建立“不可或缺性”：如卡尔霍恩所言，在一个真实的小圈子里揽下一件没人逼你、但少了你别人就会觉得不便的固定杂活。
summaries.summary_en: The greatest consensus across the panel is this: **Abundance itself is not fatal; what is fatal is that it dismantles the 'scaffolding of meaning' humans have relied on, transforming 'why we live' from an instinctual survival drive into a difficult question we must actively answer.** Whether it's Calhoun's 'depletion of roles,' Nietzsche's 'Last Man,' or Lembke's 'anhedonia,' all point to abundance eroding our forced reasons to act. The true divergence lies in how to rebuild that scaffolding. The debate centers on the path forward: Should we look inward to regain sensation through dopamine fasting, desire reduction, and mindfulness (Lembke, Epicurus, Huineng)? Should we look outward to anchor the individual through public spaces, institutional redistribution, and genuine interdependence (Arendt, Keynes, Ibn Khaldun)? Or should we take a leap upward toward self-transcendence (Nietzsche, Maslow)?
summaries.insight_en: Historical abundance mostly referred to calories and material goods, but today we face an extreme overload of cognitive and sensory signals—a paradigm shift earlier thinkers rarely anticipated. While material wealth might make the body sluggish, algorithm-driven information abundance degrades humans into passive data-consuming machines. People no longer need to fight for physical roles like Calhoun's mice, because the virtual world supplies an infinite stream of cheap, substitute achievements. **The true crisis of decline lies not in having nothing to do in the physical world, but in being stripped of the right to experience 'boredom' in the digital flood, thereby losing the very soil that nurtures spontaneous creativity.** Boredom is supposed to be the starter motor for higher-level needs; when every micro-void is filled, we lose the springboard required to reach for something greater.
summaries.advice_en: To resist decline amidst material and informational abundance, you must regain 'traction' in real life. First, **actively defend your 'boredom time' to reboot your capacity to feel.** Following Lembke’s logic, choose one day this week to spend an hour before bed or during your commute entirely screen-free. Consume zero information; let your brain cool down from high stimulation and endure the dullness until you naturally desire to initiate an action. Second, create a tangible trace: put Arendt’s theory into practice by using your hands to make something that lasts in the physical world—even if it's just assembling a chair, planting a pot, or handwriting a long letter. Third, establish indispensability: as Calhoun suggested, take on a specific, unforced chore in a small community or family where your absence would genuinely inconvenience others.

hooks.text: **位置比资源先耗尽**：一个社会最先见底的往往不是钱和物，而是可以进入的位置——岗位、住处、说话的资格。如果退缩最严重的不是最富的人而是被挡在门外的年轻人，那么关于丰裕的忧虑是不是一直问错了对象？衡量一个社会健康与否，该看它的人均产出，还是看一个新来的人要多久才能得到一个真正的位置？
hooks.text_en: **Places run out before resources**: what a society exhausts first is rarely money or goods but positions one can enter — jobs, housing, standing to speak. If the sharpest withdrawal shows up not among the richest but among the young who are locked out, has the worry about abundance been aimed at the wrong people all along? Should the health of a society be measured by output per head, or by how long it takes a newcomer to be given a real place?

hooks.text: **真角色与仪式性角色**：给人一个角色，几乎是所有人都认可的解药，可角色也能被批量制造成空的——会照开，表照填，人人被需要，却没有一件事会因为你缺席而不成立。怎么分辨自己每天做的事究竟是被真实需要，还是被制造出来让你有事做？如果一个社会靠制造角色来维持活力，它买到的是意义，还是意义的仿制品？
hooks.text_en: **Real roles and ceremonial ones**: giving people a role is the remedy almost everyone endorses, yet roles can be manufactured hollow — the meetings still held, the forms still filed, everyone needed, and nothing that would fail to happen in your absence. How do you tell whether what you do each day is genuinely required or produced so that you have something to do? And if a society sustains its vitality by manufacturing roles, has it bought meaning or an imitation of it?

hooks.text: **平线比崩塌更可能**：享乐适应让新增的好处在几周内回到基线，所以丰裕之后更可能的不是下坠，而是一条既不崩溃也不上升的平线。可平线永远不提供可见的拐点，警报因此永远不会响。什么样的指标能照出一条平线——记得住的日子有几天？做过的第一次有几件？还是别的什么？
hooks.text_en: **A flat line is likelier than a collapse**: hedonic adaptation returns any new benefit to baseline within weeks, so what follows abundance is more likely a flat line — neither crash nor climb — than a descent. But a flat line never supplies a visible inflection point, so the alarm never sounds. What kind of indicator could reveal one: how many days you can remember, how many first times you had, or something else entirely?

hooks.text: **闲暇是一种要练的能力**：产出的红利几乎全被换成了更多的东西，很少被换成时间；而少数真的拿到时间的人常发现自己不会用。我们花二十年教人谋生，却几乎不教人如何使用空出来的一天。闲暇的能力能不能被教？如果能，它该教什么——技艺、关系、独处，还是别的？
hooks.text_en: **Leisure is a skill that has to be practised**: the productivity dividend has been converted almost entirely into more things and hardly at all into time, and the few who do get the time often find they cannot use it. We spend twenty years teaching people to earn a living and almost none teaching them what to do with a day that has been cleared. Can the capacity for leisure be taught? And if it can, what would the syllabus be — a craft, relationships, solitude, something else?

hooks.text: **退缩有没有早期信号**：我把精神先于肉体的退出叫第一次死亡，可它在个体身上是逐步发生的，等到看得出来时通常已经走了很远。一个人能不能给自己查一次——最近一次对某件事有真实的胜负心是什么时候？最近一次有人具体地指望你是什么时候？这些信号该怎么读，读到了又该先动哪一步？
hooks.text_en: **Are there early signs of withdrawal**: I called the spirit's exit ahead of the body the first death, but in an individual it happens by degrees, and by the time it is visible it has usually gone a long way. Can a person run the check on himself — when did you last genuinely care whether something succeeded or failed? When did anyone last rely on you by name? How should such signs be read, and once read, which step comes first?
